steps.name: Grep for nightly-only features
steps.run:
violations=0
# Check for #![feature(...)] gates in Rust source.
if grep -rn '#!\[feature(' crates/ xtask/ --include='*.rs'; then
  echo "NFR-Test-2 / reproducible-build violation: nightly feature referenced at listed locations"
  violations=1
else
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then exit "$rc"; fi
fi
# Check for cargo +nightly references in code/config/scripts only.
# Excludes:
#   - .md   (docs may describe the forbidden pattern as spec text)
#   - .github/  (this very grep step defines the pattern as a string
#                literal; a recursive scan over .yml would self-match)
# A workflow that actually invoked `cargo +nightly` would fail at run
# time on a stable runner regardless, so the .github exclusion is safe.
if grep -rn --exclude-dir=.github 'cargo +nightly' . --include='*.yml' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.sh' --include='*.toml'; then
  echo "NFR-Test-2 / reproducible-build violation: cargo +nightly referenced at listed locations"
  violations=1
else
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then exit "$rc"; fi
fi
# Check for RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP. Same scope rationale as above.
if grep -rn --exclude-dir=.github 'RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP' . --include='*.rs' --include='*.toml' --include='*.yml' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.sh'; then
  echo "NFR-Test-2 / reproducible-build violation: RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP referenced at listed locations"
  violations=1
else
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then exit "$rc"; fi
fi
if [ "$violations" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi
echo "No nightly-only features detected."

steps.name: Pack exact producer fixtures, tools and identity
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, pathlib, shutil, subprocess, tarfile
root = pathlib.Path(os.environ['GITHUB_WORKSPACE']).resolve()
bundle = pathlib.Path(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP']) / 'ci-test-files'
tree = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD^{tree}'], text=True).strip()
manifest_path = root / 'target/maos-fixtures/manifest.json'
manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
assert manifest['schema'] == 3, manifest['schema']
# Archive extraction can replace the profile's runner with a different
# family build. Keep the fixture's verified bytes at an immutable path;
# profile_binary entries (maosctl/worker fixtures) stay profile-coupled.
runner = manifest['fixtures']['maos-wasm-runner']
stable_runner = root / 'target/maos-fixtures/maos-wasm-runner'
shutil.copy2(runner['path'], stable_runner)
runner['path'] = str(stable_runner)
entries = [f'    {json.dumps(name)}: {json.dumps(entry, separators=(",", ":"))}'
           for name, entry in sorted(manifest['fixtures'].items())]
manifest_path.write_text(
    '{\n  "schema": 3,\n  "command": ' + json.dumps(manifest['command']) +
    ',\n  "fixtures": {\n' + ',\n'.join(entries) + '\n  }\n}\n')
paths = {manifest_path, root / 'target/debug/maos',
         root / 'target/debug/maos-wasm-runner',
         root / 'target/tmp/cgroup-ceiling-fixture'}
for name, entry in manifest['fixtures'].items():
    assert entry.get('tree') == tree and entry.get('artifact'), (name, entry)
    artifact = subprocess.check_output(
        ['git', 'hash-object', '--no-filters', '--', entry['path']], cwd=root, text=True).strip()
    assert artifact == entry['artifact'], (name, entry)
    paths.add(pathlib.Path(entry['path']))
if os.environ['BUNDLE_ARCH'] == 'x64':
    paths.add(root / 'target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug/worker-probe-fixture')
with tarfile.open(bundle / 'fixtures-debug.tar', 'w') as archive:
    for path in sorted(paths):
        assert path.is_file(), str(path)
        archive.add(path, arcname=str(path).lstrip('/'), recursive=False)
with tarfile.open(bundle / 'tools.tar', 'w') as archive:
    for name in ('cargo-nextest', 'wasm-tools'):
        path = shutil.which(name)
        assert path, name
        archive.add(path, arcname=name, recursive=False)
identity = dict(sha=os.environ['GITHUB_SHA'], run_id=os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ID'],
                arch=os.environ['BUNDLE_ARCH'], workspace=str(root), tree=tree,
                nextest='0.9.149')

PY

steps.name: Decide whether the diff is platform-sensitive
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
emit() {
  local reason="${2//[$'\n\r']/ }"   # a path can carry a newline; never let it forge an output
  echo "applicable=$1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "reason=$reason" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "macos-scope: applicable=$1 — $reason"
  echo "- macos-check applicable=$1 — $reason" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
}
# Pull request: `github.sha` is the MERGE commit checkout builds, and
# its first parent is the base tip it lands on. `pull_request.base.sha`
# is NOT used: it is not refreshed when `main` moves, so diffing
# against it would charge the PR for every commit merged since it opened.
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
  BASE_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${HEAD_SHA}^1" || true)"
fi
# FAIL OPEN: with no usable base (new branch, force-push, unreachable
# commit) the diff is unknown, and an unknown diff runs the guard.
if [ -z "${BASE_SHA:-}" ] || [[ "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^0+$ ]] || ! git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  emit true "no usable diff base — guard runs (fail open)"
  exit 0
fi
# NUL-separated, so no path is ever C-quoted or split (a non-ASCII
# `macos.rs` directory must still match). Deleted paths are listed
# too (a deleted `macos.rs` is a macOS change).
list="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$list"' EXIT
git diff -z --name-only --no-renames "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" > "$list"
mapfile -d '' -t listed < "$list"
# Trees that are NOT workspace members (their own fuzz/guest/fixture/
# spike workspaces; `templates/` is `exclude`d): no change there can
# alter what `cargo check --workspace` compiles, so they never start a
# macOS runner (D-15-4-F). The contract test pins that no workspace
# member falls under this pattern. Rules (1) and (3) read `files`.
OUTSIDE_RE='^(spikes|templates|tests/fixtures|xtask/tests/fixtures)/|/(fuzz|guests|test-fixtures)/'
files=()
for f in ${listed[@]+"${listed[@]}"}; do
  [[ "$f" =~ $OUTSIDE_RE ]] || files+=("$f")
done

# (1) Named platform-sensitive paths — epic-20 §20-6 AC1, plus the
#     inputs that change what compiles: build scripts, cargo config and
#     the pinned toolchain.
PATH_RE='(^|/)macos\.rs$|^crates/maos-kernel-core/src/security/sandbox/|^crates/maos-bin/src/(purge|operator_door)\.rs$|^crates/maos-wasm-host/src/(recall_wire|codec)\.rs$|^crates/maos-frame-codec/|(^|/)Cargo\.(toml|lock)$|(^|/)build\.rs$|(^|/)\.cargo/|^rust-toolchain\.toml$|^\.github/workflows/release\.yml$'
for f in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
  if [[ "$f" =~ $PATH_RE ]]; then
    emit true "platform-sensitive path changed: $f"
    exit 0
  fi
done

# (2) This job's own definition, so a change to the guard is exercised
#     by the PR that makes it: (a) the macos-scope/macos-check job
#     blocks differ between base and head (any edit, not just one that
#     spells "macos"), or (b) any other discipline.yml line that
#     mentions macos/darwin changed. The many unrelated edits to this
#     file do not start a macOS runner.
macos_jobs() {
  git show "$1:.github/workflows/discipline.yml" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '/^  macos-(scope|check):/ {p=1; print; next} /^  (#|[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:)/ {p=0} p'
}
if [ "$(macos_jobs "$BASE_SHA")" != "$(macos_jobs "$HEAD_SHA")" ]; then
  emit true "the macos-scope/macos-check job definitions changed"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$(git diff -U0 --no-renames "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" -- .github/workflows/discipline.yml | grep -Eic '^[+-].*(macos|darwin)' || true)" -gt 0 ]; then
  emit true "discipline.yml changed a macos/darwin line"
  exit 0
fi

# (3) Rust source that is platform-conditional, or that calls OS-typed
#     APIs (`st_dev` is `dev_t`: u64 on Linux, i32 on macOS — the
#     purge.rs break had no cfg at the failing sites). Judged on the
#     file as it will be (HEAD) AND on its removed/added lines, so
#     deleting the last `cfg` from a file still counts (the `+`/`-`
#     prefix is cut first, so the anchored alternative below sees the
#     line as written). CFG_RE is line-oriented, so it also matches the
#     bare predicate lines rustfmt leaves when it wraps `#[cfg(any(…))]`
#     over several lines. API_RE matches `os::{unix,linux,fd,macos,…}`
#     wherever it sits in a path (`use std::{io, os::linux::…}`), and
#     names every crate a workspace manifest takes only under
#     `cfg(target_os = "linux")` (absent, or empty, on macOS); the
#     contract test derives that list from the manifests.
# BLIND SPOT, stated: a portable edit (a rename in a file with no
# platform marker) that breaks UNCHANGED macOS-only code elsewhere is
# not seen — that is what the pre-tag rehearsal is for.
CFG_RE='cfg(_attr)?!?\(.*(unix|windows)|\btarget_(os|family|vendor|env|arch|pointer_width|endian)[[:space:]]*=|^[[:space:]]*(not\()?(unix|windows)\)*,?[[:space:]]*$'
API_RE='(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])os::(unix|linux|fd|macos|darwin|windows)\b|std::os::\{|libc::|rustix::|nix::|MetadataExt|/proc/|landlock::|seccompiler::|maos_exec_deps::'
SRC_RE="$CFG_RE|$API_RE"
for f in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
  case "$f" in *.rs) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  git cat-file -e "$HEAD_SHA:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  if [ "$(git show "$HEAD_SHA:$f" | grep -Ec "$SRC_RE" || true)" -gt 0 ]; then
    emit true "platform-sensitive Rust source changed: $f"
    exit 0
  fi
done
for f in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
  case "$f" in *.rs) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  if [ "$(git --literal-pathspecs diff -U0 --no-renames "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" -- "$f" | grep -E '^[-+]' | grep -Ev '^(\+\+\+|---)' | cut -c2- | grep -Ec "$SRC_RE" || true)" -gt 0 ]; then
    emit true "a changed Rust line adds or removes platform-conditional code: $f"
    exit 0
  fi
done
emit false "no platform-sensitive path in this diff — NOT a pass; the pre-tag rehearsal stays mandatory"

steps.name: macOS guard disposition (Story 20-6 AC3)
steps.run:
case "$CHECK_RESULT" in
  success)
    line="macos-check: RAN and PASSED — $SCOPE_REASON" ;;
  skipped)
    if [ "$SCOPE_APPLICABLE" = "false" ]; then
      line="macos-check: NOT APPLICABLE (not a pass) — $SCOPE_REASON. The pre-tag rehearsal (docs/release/tag-procedure.md step 6) stays mandatory."
    elif [ "$SCOPE_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
      line="macos-check: NOT RUN because macos-scope was $SCOPE_RESULT — that failure already reds this aggregate."
    else
      # Applicable, yet skipped: the guard did not run. Recorded as an
      # output and failed by the LAST step, so the PR comment (which
      # sits between) is still refreshed instead of left stale.
      line="macos-check: SKIPPED although macos-scope judged it applicable ($SCOPE_REASON) — the guard did not run; this reds the aggregate."
      echo "unran=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    fi ;;
  *)
    line="macos-check: $CHECK_RESULT — $SCOPE_REASON" ;;
esac
echo "$line"
echo "$line" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

steps.name: Check for failures
steps.run:
# macos-check is the ONLY skipped-job exemption; its 20-6 disposition step owns applicability.
failed=$(jq -r 'to_entries | any(.value.result == "failure" or .value.result == "cancelled" or (.key != "macos-check" and .value.result == "skipped"))' <<< "$NEEDS_JSON")
if [[ "$failed" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "overall=failure" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
else
  echo "overall=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
fi
